chunks: To Him is your return all together; [it is] the promise of Allah [which is] true. Indeed, He begins creation; then He repeats it so that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds in justice. But for those who disbelieved is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
ai.seo_question: What is the promise of Allah regarding the return of creation and the fate of believers and disbelievers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the inevitability of the Ma'ad (Resurrection) as a divine promise, linking the initial creation (al-bad') with the return (al-i'ada) to demonstrate Allah's power over life and death. It highlights that the disbelievers' punishment is a direct consequence of their persistent denial (kufr), while believers receive their due reward with perfect justice (al-qist), reflecting the attribute of Adl.
